items.note: The plan gives the constants, both gate sets, the eight-row schedule, the net change (JV+RG)x independent of scratch values, both coefficient cancellations, the three stages (x,y+x),(-y,y+x),(-y,x) and the wire counts W_b, W_c. This is the proof at 741-783 step by step.

The plan states D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}. It derives it by the stored-equals-frame-of-logical invariant, with sources by definition, edges by D_vD_u^{-1} and gates by commuting with a common frame, then reads off eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} per route. This is the paper's argument.

Present with correct content: the bilinear forms, the terminal labels, the stage transitions A',P',B', the gate-label table, the 2->5 side edge as the use of orthogonality, the single decrease 3->4 of h, L=Ich, telescoping to Wm-2N+2L, and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539 below 1/2. Two small slips are listed as errors (the S4.3 header's 'below N/2' and the 'coordinate unit' parenthetical in S4.3.4.5). The full edge-residual table and the plane-absorption proof of orthonormal bases are summarized, not reproduced.

The plan assigns projections P_U and -P_{U_a}, uses frames Phi_M, and gets rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U. It covers the N exceptional source edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one and the endpoint check P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m, then s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m. This matches the proof at 1156-1172.

The plan follows the paper's route: weight additivity mod 4 for orthogonal vectors, the phase difference as a sum over the residual basis with odd weights, and each character turned into the kernel aI+bX_v by Hadamard conjugation. It then fixes the X_a->Y_a pair (C^{-1} on 27 coordinates, Z_{a,k} and i^{27k}) and negates the X outputs. s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c with deficit 2N-2L_c.

The plan has L/N<1/2, s_b<W_b m and s_c<W_c m, and the exact deficits 339/22587335000000 and 73/19906842167500, both >20*2^{-50}. It uses log m<20 and m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50})>m(1-eta) to get s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, which is the argument at 1319-1346.

S2 lists the elementary scans correctly. S3 states the controlled shift with its split-and-merge mechanism, but it drops the lemma's hypothesis that the offset be preparable in b^{O(1)} time (and the prime-radix and unit conditions), so it reads as unconditional. Two infer steps without a sub-derivation count as stated.

The plan follows the paper's derivation: factorization A=E1 Pi E2 by topmost-row/rightmost-entry elimination, an odd prime avoiding the table's denominators, lower-triangular transforms as controlled shifts in descending order, and each one of Pi done by D+=H, an interchange, then D=H-D, so a ones cost a interchanges.

Every step of the paper's proof is there: the cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, Phi_{A_e} per edge by recursive interchanges, the frame identity giving Phi_{I_m}f_w and H<-H+D on every row, and the three-shear interchange. It also has s calls per node, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), the geometric sum split a<=1 or a>1, and the fixed-tape parking/descriptor schedule with its O(V) and descriptor bounds.

The plan covers k and rho, the field-order sequence, row range q^{2rho}>=W^k, padding to R'<2R, the base-m split costing O(V) sum a_j m^{j tau}=O(Ve^tau), padding [2^u] to [q^e], and one-bit-unequal widths, as in the proof.

The plan has H_0=bSCS, C^2=X, C^{-1}=-iZCZ, conjugation by P_M with the residual basis as first columns, slots of f chunks with one child (C^{eps})^{tensor f} per residual vector, and inverse children from one forward call. It also has the m(m-1)+3m row additions, s_c children on e/m axes, and H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D.

The plan follows the proof closely: the eight conditional updates with cycles (00 01 10) and (01 10 11), the output (u+c(1-2(u mod 2)),w), guard segments, one cyclic shift per line, the bad set with guards 10..2^{K-1}-11 and delta_bad=80(f-1)2^{-K}, and T0 S0^{-1} permuting B. It also covers the swap+rotation implementation, the radix-sort repair, the full cost and its o(1) simplification, and the application to a basis change at O(V((eK)^tau+1)).

Covered: individual kernels at O(Ve), node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)), q_0 row chunks with R_row>=W^{k0}, the role split u=Wg+w giving exact V/W children, exponent conditions, F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), the internal sum O(e^lambda), leaves O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}), and base-m pieces giving O(d^{lambda'}). S4.6.3.2 words the node overhead loosely; this is listed as an error.

Covered: the guard-width constants E, B, nu, C_1=20, C_0=128mB^2, the depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E with concatenated calls, A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1}, the total below C_0 d^{C_1}, the 2^{-(p+l)} grid with modulus 2^l, and Delta=o(p). The proposition's proof (uniform packed-call cost, Q_p(Hz) in O(Vd^{lambda'}), error <sqrt2 2^{-p} since H has absolute row sums one) is also there.

The plan covers character cancellation via the shift by t/2^{v+1}, the DIF recursion, bit-reversed storage B_t, the reverse procedure giving F^+B^{-1}, grouped rounds H then J_E, and the layout L (prefix slots, Dq-1 chunk exchanges). It also has the round costs, J_E commuting with truncation, the error sqrt2 l 2^{-p}, and LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}.

The plan covers B_0=2^{4p}, |A_u|<B_0^r/2, |h_j|<B_0/2, two's-complement block packing, centered-residue extraction via the residual identity, negacyclic reduction with |H_j|<=r2^{2p}, a right shift by p+l, and four products at O(rp log(rp)), as in the proof.

The plan has the retained LB order (pointwise product commutes with a common record permutation), F^-(f*g)=M F^-f F^-g and F^+F^-=I/M, and the error chain 2delta+eta, then 3delta+eta, then M(3delta+eta)=sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p}, with the stated cost.

The plan has P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA via the Gaussian maps S, T, N=CTD with ||N-I||<1/2, the normalizations S', J', D', and the left inverse D N^{-1} C. S6.1 omits the side hypotheses p>100 and alpha>=2, which is not material here.

The plan has periodicity of a, the coefficient comparison leaving exp(2 pi i sum s_i j_i k_i/t_i), Q reading frequency -s_i j_i, F_q^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F_q^+ giving RF^+R=F^+, and the two normalizations giving (u*v)/S^2. This is the proof at 3938-3988. Conjugation for RF^+ is in S8.5.4.

All fixed rationals, sizes, alpha, gamma, eta, the Rosser-Schoenfeld interval count, the choice of odd primes, T/2<S<T by Bernoulli, alpha^4 theta_i>p, t_i<2^p and the n^{o(1)} prime search match the paper.

The plan covers the isomorphism via the order-S image of x, the triangular coordinates b_i, padding in one nested scan, updates in order i=d..1 as prefix-controlled rotations preserving the valid set, and O(d^2) unequal-width axis moves at O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)).

The plan covers well-definedness (zeta y)^r=1, the diagonal invertible map with sup-norm preservation, the wrap factor zeta^j, M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T, and the computed version with twist factors of error <2*2^{-p}.

The chirp transform, the source transform with exact counterpart 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A=RF_s, F^+ by conjugation, the digit preparation, the six steps and the role of the two scales S are all correct. S8's headline adds that the product is obtained 'in O(Tp) steps beyond the layer costs', which misstates the cost structure (Gaussian maps, CRT layouts and packed products are superlinear). Graded imprecise to be conservative.

The error chain E_ring<5TL, 6TL, 8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL matches, with norm margins .51/.701/.501. So do (2E_s+2), (3E_s+2), E_w<28*2^gamma T^2 L, the final bound 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2 using gamma<=b/4, the rounding, and the carry recurrence with its bounds and invariant.

Covered: V=Tp, the seven table rows and their powers, the margins g_1..g_7 with min 2^{-181}=2kappa, the row justifications, setup p^{A+C}=o(Tp), exceptional streams O(Vp^{A'}2^{-K})=o(V), a fixed power of log p <= p^kappa, O(n(log n)^{1-kappa}), and the schoolbook cutoff.

S1 recalls that Schonhage-Strassen proposed n log n as optimal and that a strict power saving is obtained. No step states what an eventual lower bound means (T_A(n)>=c_A n lg n for every machine) or that one machine with liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n)=0 negates it.

errors.says: the total dimension L lost on decreasing edges is L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, below N/2
errors.paper: The bound is on L, L<N/2, equivalently L/N<1/2 (lines 895, 1105-1110). The header writes the ratio L/N and says it is below N/2, which is the wrong comparison.

errors.says: every nonzero residual is nondegenerate and nonalternating (it contains a coordinate unit vector of norm one)
errors.paper: The residual contains a norm-one vector built by tensoring norm-one vectors from each summand: coordinate units in B, Q^perp and the triple complements, and the line generators of P and Q. It places the result in one orthogonal summand. This is generally not a coordinate unit vector of F^{tensor 3}.

errors.says: At a node with e=m^k chunks, the s children plus binary basis changes, scalar gates, endpoint corrections and reassembly cost O(V((eK)^tau+1)) at that node.
errors.paper: Only the non-recursive work (basis changes and inverses, scalar gates, endpoint corrections, reassembly) costs O(V((eK)^tau+1)). The s child calls cost s(V/W)F(e/m) on top of that, which S4.6.3.7 states correctly.

errors.says: obtaining the exact 2n-bit product in O(Tp) steps beyond the layer costs
errors.paper: Outside the butterfly layers the normalized costs include Gaussian line maps dp^{1/2+delta}alpha, CRT and axis layouts d^2(1+l^tau), chirps dp^delta and packed products log(rp), all superlinear in Tp. Only input conversion, padding, carries and output are O(Tp).

errors.says: an update y->y+a(controls) (mod Q) of a target field following its control fields costs O(V)
errors.paper: The lemma assumes a fixed prime radix q, denominators prime to q, and an offset preparable in b^{O(1)} time from the controls. The plan states the cost without the offset condition.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route from start to finish. It builds the scalar exchange network, the common-frame identity and the nested labels, which give s<Wm. That feeds the bit interface, then the matrix shear, the power-width interchange recurrence and the arbitrary-width swap. In parallel it feeds the complex phase interface, then the phase-frame recursion, packed basis changes, the layer recurrence and the guard widths. From there it runs through synthetic transforms, ring convolution, resampling, chirp cancellation, CRT, the algorithm, exact recovery and the cost table with margin 2kappa. It thins only at the final 'disproving' step, which is only alluded to, and at loose cost wording in S8 and S4.6.3.2. Neither breaks the chain.

steps.note: h=100, v=binom(h,3), N=v^3, m=h^3, banks indexed by a in T^3, three stages giving (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and restoring every scratch wire whatever its initial value.
A common frame per gate commutes with the pointwise gate, so the network implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}. Each edge pays only D_vD_u^{-1}, and the endpoint frames fix the route operator.

Nondegenerate labels in F^{tensor 3} of dimension m, built from triple indicators that are orthogonal for neighbors. Every edge joins comparable labels, and the only decrease is the central edge 3->4, which loses h.
P_V-P_U is the identity on V cap U^perp with rank dim V-dim U, and the N source edges 2P_{U_a} are the rank-one exceptions.
L=Ich and sum |Delta dim|=Wm-2N+2L by telescoping at gates. Adding N gives s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.

L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539 are both below 1/2. The extra N source ranks still leave a strict saving, so s_b<W_b m, and the complex deficit is 2N-2L_c>0. The bit deficit N-2L_b is conveyed in words rather than written out.
M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m holds on every role (P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m for X_a, 0 to I otherwise), so the bit network applies H<-H+D on every row, scratch rows included.
A=E1 Pi E2, triangular parts at O(V), and each one of Pi as one interchange, so a rank-a shear costs a interchanges plus O(V). The node makes s recursive calls.
Children of volume V/W give F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1). Then s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}, from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20, and the geometric sum gives F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: The plan rebuilds the whole central chain with its defining content: the fixed h=100 exchange network, the frame identity, nested labels with the single decrease of h, rank equal to dimension change with the N rank-one source exceptions, the budget Wm-2N+2L and s_b, the ratios 100/539 and 101/539 below 1/2, the endpoint identity, rank-a shears as a interchanges, and the recurrence to e^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}. All nine steps are reconstructed. The only blemish is the S4.3 header's mis-stated comparison 'below N/2'.
